precepts.text: That the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not follow a multitude to do evil. Enter not into the path of the wicked; sinners entice, saying come with us, cast in thy lot among us, but walk not thou in the way with them, for their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood. Many of our young men's lives end short because they follow a multitude to do evil. To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of; a soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins.

note.label: Exodus 23: Righteous Judgment, the Three Feasts, and the Angel of the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Also, that the soul be without knowledge, it is not good; and he that hasteth with his feet sinneth.”

To be in the midst of the singing, like the whole school hollering fight, fight, fight, is to be in the multitude the Most High warns of. A soul without knowledge of the laws of God hastes with his feet and sins; he runs with the crowd because he does not know the law says not to follow a multitude to do evil.

precepts.text: Houses and riches are the inheritance of fathers, and a prudent wife is from the Lord.
precepts.point: It is important for us to build our legacy and pass it down; that is one of the things we lack in Israel today. Some of us use captivity as an excuse not to better ourselves or build, but that is not what the scriptures say: get the job, further your education, do more for yourself, your family, and the body. Building up your house also means spiritually building it, teaching your wife and children.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
“House and riches are the inheritance of fathers: and a prudent wife is from the Lord.” Houses and riches are what fathers pass down; that is the inheritance a man is supposed to leave, and a prudent wife is from the Lord.

That is the rest Naomi wished for her daughters in law, each in the house of her husband. Building up your house means the inheritance, and it also means spiritually building it, teaching your wife and children.

precepts.text: There are many devices in a man's heart, but the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.
precepts.point: Absalom and all the men of Israel said Hushai's counsel was better than Ahithophel's. The Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that He might bring evil upon Absalom. The Lord was working with Hushai and David, while Satan was in the spirit of Absalom and Ahithophel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.”

Ahithophel had his device and Hushai had his. “And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel.” But it was not Absalom’s choosing that decided it: “For the Lord had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the Lord might bring evil upon Absalom.” The counsel of the Lord stood.

There is safety in a multitude of counselors, but only where the counsel is according to thus saith the Lord. A counselor who does not go to the scriptures is not one you should want.

precepts.text: Smite a scorner and the simple will beware; the scorner is called simple, and these words are synonymous.
precepts.point: Making wise the simple: pay attention to who the simple is, the scorner, the foolish, the youth void of understanding. A lot of times we go out and think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but it also goes into a youth who thinks he knows something but really does not.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” Pay attention to who the simple is. “Smite a scorner, and the simple will beware: and reprove one that hath understanding, and he will understand knowledge.”

Smite a scorner and the simple will beware: the scorner is called simple. These words are synonymous. A lot of times we think the scorner is somebody who does not want to hear, but the simple one is the same person.

precepts.text: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; that is how you preserve your soul and are delivered out of the hands of the wicked. He that despiseth His ways shall die, meaning you love evil and love sin and you will die.
precepts.point: He preserveth the souls of His saints and delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
He preserveth the souls of his saints and delivereth them out of the hand of the wicked. How? “He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; but he that despiseth his ways shall die.”

Keeping the commandment is how you preserve your soul and are delivered out of the hands of the wicked. And he that despises his ways shall die: that is loving evil and loving sin, and the end of it is death.

precepts.text: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them; the owner only beholds them with his eyes.
precepts.point: Wealth makes many friends, but the poor is separated from his neighbor. When goods increase, so do those that eat them.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
“Wealth maketh many friends; but the poor is separated from his neighbour.” Money draws a crowd, and the poor man is left by himself.

Solomon says why the crowd comes: “When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good is there to the owners thereof, saving the beholding of them with their eyes?” The more a man has, the more mouths gather to eat it, and the owner himself gets nothing out of it but to look on with his eyes.

Those many friends that wealth makes are the ones increased to eat the goods. That is the friendship riches buy, and it is why the poor man walking in his integrity is better off than the perverse fool with a crowd around him.

precepts.text: Discipline must start in the youth.
precepts.point: Discipline must start in the youth. If you wait until twelve or thirteen to begin, it is over, or you will have a very difficult time.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
“Chasten thy son while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his crying.” There is a window when chastening still has hope in it, and a father is not to hold back because the child cries.

Ecclesiasticus says the same and says when: “Bow down his neck while he is young, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he wax stubborn, and be disobedient unto thee, and so bring sorrow to thine heart.” Discipline must start in the youth. If you wait until twelve or thirteen to begin, it is over, or you will have a very difficult time; by then he has waxed stubborn and disobedient, and the sorrow comes to your own heart.

Esau has continually tried to take away our ability to rightfully punish our children and bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. The law gives that right to the parent, and it gives it while there is hope.

precepts.text: The heart is deceitful above all things and desperately wicked; who can know it?
precepts.point: The fear of the Lord tends to life, and he that has it shall abide satisfied and not be visited with evil.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
“There are many devices in a man’s heart; nevertheless the counsel of the Lord, that shall stand.” A man's heart is full of its own plans and schemes, but none of them stand against the counsel of the Lord.

This is why the heart is called what it is called in Jeremiah: “The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?” Those many devices come out of a heart that deceives even the man who carries it. He cannot know his own heart, so he cannot trust the devices it makes.

That is why a man must hear counsel and receive instruction to be wise in his latter end, and why the fear of the Lord tends to life: the counsel of the Lord stands when the devices of the deceitful heart fall.

precepts.text: We were brought down to the serving class because of sin.
precepts.point: Bread, correction, and work are for a servant. We have been brought down to the serving class because of sin, because of disobedience to God's commandments.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
“Judgments are prepared for scorners, and stripes for the back of fools.” The Most High is preparing us for the kingdom, and he will beat that foolishness out of us.

Ecclesiasticus tells what is set aside for whom: “Fodder, a wand, and burdens, are for the ass; and bread, correction, and work, for a servant.” Bread, correction and work are for a servant. That is where we are: we have been brought down to the serving class because of sin, because of disobedience to God's commandments.

So the stripes for the back of fools are not random. Correction belongs to the servant, and Israel is in the servant's place until the foolishness is beaten out and we are ready for the kingdom.

precepts.text: Is Israel a servant? Is he a homeborn slave? Why is he spoiled? Because of disobedience.
precepts.point: Bread, correction, and work are for a servant. We have been brought down to the serving class because of sin, because of disobedience to God's commandments.

note.label: Proverbs 19: Discipline, the Fear of the Lord, and Servitude

precepts.why:
Bread, correction and work are for a servant, and stripes are for the back of fools. Jeremiah asks the question that goes with it: “Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?”

Israel was not made to be a slave, yet here he is spoiled, brought down to the serving class. Why? Because of disobedience to God's commandments. Sin put us under correction, and the correction is the stripes the fool's back gets.

The Most High is preparing us for the kingdom, and the servant's correction is how he beats that foolishness out of us.

precepts.text: He that keeps the commandment keeps his own soul, so you must deliver your own soul by keeping the Most High's commandments.
precepts.point: They shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness; everyone has to work out their own righteousness in fear and trembling, delivering their own soul by keeping the Most High's commandments.

note.label: Ezekiel 14: Idols in the Heart and the Four Sore Judgments

precepts.why:
“He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his own soul; but he that despiseth his ways shall die.” That is how Noah, Daniel and Job would deliver their own souls: by their righteousness, by keeping the commandment.

Even if He sends a pestilence into the land and pours out His fury upon it in blood to cut off man and beast, and though those three men were in it, “they shall deliver neither son nor daughter; they shall but deliver their own souls by their righteousness.” Nobody's righteousness covers anybody else's soul.

So everyone has to work out their own righteousness in fear and trembling. You deliver your own soul by keeping the Most High's commandments, and he that despises His ways shall die.
